PullRequest.Title: agentHost: keep open canvases across session configuration refreshes
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #340508

When a send refreshes a chat's session configuration (for example after its customizations change), the Agent Host destroys the chat's SDK session and resumes a replacement. Destroying the session cleared its canvas projection and published an empty canvas list, so the Agents window closed every open canvas, and the replacement then ignored the canvases the runtime restored.

The refresh now hands the projected canvases to the replacement:

- `CopilotAgentSession.takeCanvasProjection()` releases the old session's canvases and republishes them without a source, so they keep their resources (and their tabs) and show as temporarily unavailable.
- `CopilotAgent` holds the handoff per chat while the refresh runs. The replacement is created with it, keeps those canvases instead of ignoring them on resume, accepts the runtime's rehydration events, and reconciles them with `rpc.canvas.listOpen` once its extensions settle.
- Membership changes stay unpublished until the refresh adopts the replacement that survives restore retries. If the refresh fails, the canvases close as before.
- Canvas projection state is now one phase (`starting`, `live`, `released`) plus a per-canvas hand-over mark, replacing two flags and a parallel set.

The canvas contract in `AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md` now describes the refresh handoff.

## How to test

1. Enable `chat.canvases.enabled`. In the Agents window, start a local Copilot session in a folder.
2. Ask the agent to open a canvas.
3. Add a file such as `.github/instructions/test.instructions.md` to the folder, then send another message.

The canvas tab stays open, is briefly unavailable, and then reloads from the new runtime. Before this change, the tab closed.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --grep "canvas|config-driven session refresh"`: 29 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`: 1,731 passing, 14 failing locally. The failures are in tests unrelated to canvases and refreshes that depend on machine state, such as existing `~/.copilot/session-state` entries or a `/home/test` home directory.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSdkCanvas.integrationTest.ts`: passed, including the new test that keeps an open canvas across a resume on the real Copilot runtime.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>`: no problems.
- Manual, in a Code - OSS Agents window before rebasing onto current `main`: two consecutive refreshes, with one and then two canvases open. Every tab stayed open and reloaded from the new runtime, and the host published no empty `chat/canvasesChanged`. A canvas opened after the first refresh got its own tab.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending or resuming a turn after configuration changes while one or more canvases are open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The chat queue checks configuration, destroys the old SDK session, resumes a replacement, waits for extension readiness, then the diff awaits one canvas.listOpen RPC before initialization completes and the turn can proceed. Per-canvas state publications are synchronous local dispatches but downstream subscriber delivery is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Destroy/disconnect the old SDK session and resume a replacement runtime session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One destroy and one resume for a configuration refresh, excluding bounded restore retries
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Configuration refresh already destroyed and resumed the SDK session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must complete before the turn proceeds

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read persisted session metadata and working-directory state during resume
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped metadata/working-directory restore sequence per replacement attempt
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same metadata and workspace restoration occurred before the change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List extension/canvas registry state while waiting for canvas extensions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extensions.list and one canvas.list per canvas-enabled replacement attempt
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Replacement initialization already waited for these runtime RPCs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already awaited during initialization before the change

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the replacement runtime's complete open-canvas snapshot with rpc.canvas.listOpen
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one call per replacement attempt only when at least one handed-over canvas exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No listOpen RPC occurred during refresh initialization; the old projection was cleared instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited after extensions settle and before replacement initialization completes; bounded by the existing 30-second control-plane timeout

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish unavailable/restored CanvasStateChanged updates to subscribed clients
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most a small constant number of updates for each of at most 8 projected canvases; publications are local synchronous dispatches and subscriber transport is not awaited
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Destroying the old session removed canvas membership rather than handing channels through replacement state updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only local event dispatch is synchronous; client transport is off the awaited refresh critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The handed-over projection set is capped at 8 canvases per chat. Reconciliation examines at most those 8 projections; the listOpen response contains the runtime's open-canvas snapshot and is fetched once per replacement attempt.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh is serialized by the owning chat queue. Session destruction, resume, extension readiness, and the added listOpen call occur sequentially. There is no per-canvas RPC fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used for listOpen because reconciliation needs the replacement runtime's post-extension snapshot. With no projected canvases, the handoff is absent and reconciliation returns without the new RPC. Warm sessions that do not require configuration refresh perform no added boundary work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one added awaited IPC and bounded projection work; low confidence that its magnitude is large enough to be reportable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The latency and serialized size of listOpen depend on runtime responsiveness and the total runtime open-canvas snapshot, which is not explicitly capped by the host's 8-projection limit. The diff nevertheless adds only one grouped RPC on an already exceptional configuration-refresh path, so there is insufficient evidence of a user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added critical-path RPC is intentional reconciliation work, grouped rather than per-canvas, skipped without a handoff, and bounded in frequency by configuration refreshes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Configuration refresh whose replacement is discarded because the SDK client changes during restore
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each restore attempt fully initializes a candidate replacement, including the added handoff reconciliation, before client-generation validation can discard it and retry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch/resume and dispose candidate SDK sessions across client-replacement retries
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The bounded retry loop and full candidate initialization already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All failed attempts delay refresh completion

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional grouped RPC for each candidate, up to 5
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restore retries did not query open canvases.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 8 handed-over canvases and at most 5 serial restore attempts, as capped by MAX_SESSION_RESTORE_ATTEMPTS.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Attempts are sequential, not concurrent. Aggregate added work is at most five listOpen RPCs and bounded canvas state updates under repeated client replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The handoff is retained across attempts so each candidate must reconcile against its own runtime; no candidate result is reusable after client replacement. No negative cache is relevant.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in serial retry multiplicity and the five-attempt cap.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Five attempts are possible only when the SDK client is repeatedly replaced during restore, an exceptional condition. Individual RPC latency is runtime-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff adds repeated work under retries, but retries are exceptional, strictly capped, and serialized; no concurrency burst or unbounded amplification is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Configuration refresh with no currently projected canvases, and ordinary cold create/resume outside a refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session initialization still calls the reconciliation helper after extension readiness, but it returns immediately because no handed-over projection exists.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extensions.list and one canvas.list for canvas-enabled session initialization
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical boundary work occurred before the change.

Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The absence of a handoff acts as the negative state and avoids listOpen entirely; no stale cache or repeated miss is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the handoff guard and call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added local empty-map check is constant and negligible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The common no-handoff path adds no boundary call, retention, or meaningful allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh failure after the old canvas projection has been released
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The old session hands off at most 8 projection records, replacement creation fails, and the finally block removes the handoff and publishes canvas membership removal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish removal of canvas membership after failed replacement
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One membership action for the chat
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Destroying the prior session cleared membership during disposal instead of at handoff settlement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous local publication during finally; subscriber transport is not awaited

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 8 projections retained only for the duration of the refresh.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cleanup runs synchronously in the refresh finally block; no background retry or parallel owner remains.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The ResourceMap entry is deleted only if it still owns the same handoff, preventing an older settlement from deleting a newer handoff. Failed handoffs are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that both the agent-level handoff map and failed candidate session are released through finally/disposal paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material because retained state and cleanup cardinality are hard-capped.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The change preserves bounded cleanup ownership and does not introduce unbounded retention.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed files and every diff hunk for performance. Traced configuration-refresh sends/resumes, canvas-enabled initialization, bounded restore retries, subscriber state publication, and failure cleanup. The only new expensive boundary is one grouped canvas.listOpen IPC per replacement attempt when a handoff exists; it is serial, skipped without canvases, and paired with at most eight projections. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
